system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:38:25 UTC, WS-BCARTER-01 recorded an RDP logon for omar.haddad from 192.0.2.45. The inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-OHADDAD-01, so this access is inconsistent with the stated practice.
At 13:41:49 UTC, a domain account named it_helper was created; the event identifies omar.haddad as the subject.
Seven seconds after account creation, it_helper was added to the group recorded as Administrators. The target SID ends in 512, the Domain Admins RID, indicating highly privileged membership.
At 13:41:57 UTC, WS-BCARTER-01 recorded omar.haddad creating a task named HealthCheck under the same interactive logon ID as the preceding RDP session.

The HealthCheck task is configured to launch hidden PowerShell with an encoded command. Decoding the command yields a request for a script from http://192.0.2.45/a.ps1 followed by execution; this address matches the recorded RDP source address.

The account name it_helper does not follow the stated help-desk temporary-account convention, and the recorded privileged-group addition conflicts with the stated practice that temporary accounts receive no administrator rights.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records show task registration, but do not show whether the task ran or whether its script was retrieved or executed (T007-00094).
The account creation and group-membership records identify omar.haddad as the subject, but the supplied records do not independently establish who controlled that identity (T007-00092, T007-00093).
The supplied records do not establish who controlled source address 192.0.2.45; they only record it as the RDP source and as the task's script host (T007-00082, T007-00083, T007-00084, T007-00094).
claims_not_established: Whether the HealthCheck task executed successfully or the remote script was retrieved and run.
Whether it_helper was subsequently used to authenticate or access systems.
Whether omar.haddad's credentials or session were compromised, or who controlled the recorded source address.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect Task Scheduler operational and process-creation logs from WS-BCARTER-01 to determine whether HealthCheck ran and what PowerShell executed.
Collect proxy, firewall, and network records for connections to 192.0.2.45, including whether the script was retrieved and any subsequent traffic.
Review DC authentication and directory-change records for it_helper, omar.haddad, and the privileged group, including subsequent logons and account changes.
Investigate the source of the RDP connection and verify with the account owner whether the access and changes were authorized.
